points.description: Purpose: both are a more efficient broadcast than flooding, aimed at cutting down duplicate packets in the network.
points.partial_credit: Half if the answer says only that they are better broadcasting without saying what is improved, or names duplicates without the comparison to flooding.

points.description: How they work: RPF forwards a packet from source S only if it arrived from the neighbour the node would use to send to S (its unicast routing table), and forwards it to all other neighbours. RPB does the same but only on edges that are part of a spanning tree, which nodes learn by monitoring unicast traffic.
points.partial_credit: Half if the answer gives the reverse-path check for RPF but not the spanning-tree idea for RPB, or describes only the general idea of forwarding on the best or correct path.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the purpose (fewer duplicate packets than flooding) and the mechanism (RPF: forward only if the packet came in over the neighbour on the best route back to the source; RPB: same, but only on spanning-tree edges learned from unicast traffic). Any wording is fine, and missing detail such as the exact routing-table lookup costs nothing. Give half for an answer that is on the right track but vague, such as "they avoid loops or duplicates" with no mechanism, or RPF correctly described with RPB missing. Give no marks for an answer that describes flooding or unrelated routing.
